text: well, i dont think its that complicated, the fact of the matter is my approach is rather simple i just pick N amount of triangles that are even in a vertical range, 2-4-6-8-10 and then create strips, everything on that horizontal axis basically inherits it and then go againe, basically sticking to existing curvature in the model so that it retains shape, [Image #1] see its pretty simple actually
resolution: Refined the proposed teach-by-demonstration retopology into the user's actual simpler workflow: a deterministic quad-strip propagation operator. An even contiguous vertical seed of 2/4/6/8/10 triangles defines the pairing cadence; the operator walks horizontally across adjacent columns, repeats the same topology pattern without moving vertices so existing curvature is retained, previews the result, and stops at poles/fans, boundaries, seams, odd/mismatched columns, or non-manifold topology for a manual reseed. Proposed exposing the same selection-driven operator to humans and Agent Seat rather than building a generalized learned retopology system. No code changed in this design clarification.
